1. 🏛️ REGULATORY BODIES & FINANCIAL MARKET FRAMEWORKS

CAPITAL MARKETS & REGULATORY № 1

IFSCA Notifies Market Abuse Regulations 2026 in GIFT IFSC: Replaces SEBI PIT and PFUTP Regimes

  • Genesis & Regulatory Autonomy: The International Financial Services Centres Authority (IFSCA) notified the IFSCA (Market Abuse) Regulations, 2026, establishing a dedicated statutory framework to prevent insider trading, market manipulation, and unlawful disclosure of inside information in GIFT City.
  • Dismantling Domestic SEBI Regime:
    • From the date of commencement, domestic SEBI regulations—namely the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading / PIT) Regulations, 2015 and SEBI (Prohibition of Fraudulent and Unfair Trade Practices / PFUTP) Regulations, 2003—will no longer apply within IFSC.
    • IFSCA assumes exclusive regulatory and enforcement jurisdiction over all securities listed or traded on IFSC exchanges.
  • Mandatory Trade Disclosure Threshold:
    • Designated persons and insiders must disclose quarterly trades exceeding $25,000 within 2 business days to the compliance officer and the exchange.
  • Statutory Enforcement Powers:
    • Empowers IFSCA to issue formal warnings, censures, monetary penalties, disgorgement of illegal profits, and suspension or cancellation of registration of intermediaries and listed entities under Section 12 & Section 13 of the IFSCA Act, 2019.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Regulatory Replacement: Replaces SEBI PIT 2015 and SEBI PFUTP 2003 in IFSC.
  • Quarterly Disclosure Threshold: Trades above $25,000 within 2 business days (crucial numerical question).
  • Governing Law: IFSCA Act, 2019 (HQ: GIFT City, Gandhinagar; Chairperson: K. Rajaraman).
  • Target MCQ Form: "Under the newly notified IFSCA Market Abuse Regulations 2026, what is the trade disclosure threshold for designated persons?" → Trades exceeding $25,000 within 2 business days.
CAPITAL MARKETS & REGULATORY № 2

PFRDA Mandates 5 Equity-Based Risk Categories for NPS Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF)

  • Standardised Risk Classification: The Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) introduced a uniform 5-tier classification system for all schemes under the Multiple Scheme Framework (MSF) to simplify subscriber comparison.
  • The 5 Mandated Equity Categories:
    • Category A: 80%–100% Equity allocation → Aggressive Growth / Very High Risk
    • Category B: 60%–80% Equity allocation → High Growth / High Risk
    • Category C: 35%–60% Equity allocation → Balanced Growth / Medium Risk
    • Category D: 10%–35% Equity allocation → Conservative Growth / Low to Medium Risk
    • Category E: 0%–10% Equity allocation → Debt-oriented / Low Risk
  • Portfolio Restructuring: All existing Pension Fund Managers (PFMs) are mandated to restructure and rename their existing MSF offerings to strictly adhere to these prescribed equity bands and risk nomenclatures.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Highest Equity Slab (Category A): 80%–100% (Aggressive / Very High Risk).
  • Debt-Oriented Slab (Category E): 0%–10% equity.
  • Regulator: PFRDA (administered under PFRDA Act, 2013; HQ: New Delhi).
  • Target MCQ Form: "Under the PFRDA Multiple Scheme Framework revamp, which category corresponds to a 60%–80% equity allocation?" → Category B (High Growth / High Risk).
CAPITAL MARKETS & REGULATORY № 3

SEBI Eases Compliance Norms for Category-I FPIs Investing 100% in Government Securities

  • Targeted Regulatory Relief: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) relaxed granular disclosure and operational norms for Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) investing solely in sovereign debt.
  • Eligibility & Exemption Conditions:
    • Applies exclusively to Category-I FPIs that allocate 100% of their assets under custody (AUC) into Government Securities (G-Secs), State Development Loans (SDLs), and Treasury Bills (T-Bills).
    • Exempts eligible sovereign debt FPIs from providing granular beneficial ownership (BO) disclosures mandated under the August 2023 anti-circumvention framework.
    • Substantially lowers compliance turnaround time to encourage foreign capital inflows into fully accessible route (FAR) sovereign bonds post-J.P. Morgan and Bloomberg-EM index inclusion.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Eligible Segment: Category-I FPIs with 100% G-Sec / Sovereign debt holdings.
  • Exempted Requirement: Granular Beneficial Ownership (BO) look-through reporting.
  • Regulatory Anchor: Promulgated under SEBI (Foreign Portfolio Investors) Regulations, 2019.
CAPITAL MARKETS & REGULATORY № 4

SEBI Proposes Net Settlement for Mutual Fund Scheme Cash Trades & Extends Angel Fund Accredited Norms

  • Cash Market Net Settlement Proposal:
    • SEBI issued a consultation paper proposing net settlement of funds across mutual fund schemes within the cash market segment.
    • Replaces gross scheme-level fund settlement, eliminating redundant liquidity fragmentation and mitigating overnight intraday capital drag for Asset Management Companies (AMCs).
  • Angel Fund Accredited Investor Mandate Extension:
    • Extended the compliance deadline for Angel Funds to ensure all contributing investors satisfy the accredited investor framework.
    • Existing portfolio investments will remain protected and grandfathered under their original Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) agreements.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Core Mechanism: Shift from gross settlement to net settlement of funds for MF schemes in cash equity.
  • Angel Funds: Accredited investor compliance transition extended while grandfathering existing PPMs.
CAPITAL MARKETS & REGULATORY № 5

SEBI and European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) Sign Landmark CCP Cooperation MoU

  • Cross-Border Market Infrastructure Accord: SEBI and the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) executed a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding on Central Counterparties (CCPs).
  • Strategic Significance & Trade Clearing:
    • Establishes formal supervisory cooperation and information-exchange protocols regarding qualified Indian Central Counterparties clearing trades for European banks and institutions.
    • Mitigates systemic regulatory friction and ensures uninterrupted cross-border capital flow between the European Union and the Indian clearing ecosystem (Clearing Corporation of India / CCIL).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Bilateral Counterparts: SEBI (India) and ESMA (European Union).
  • Subject Matter: Supervision, equivalence, and information sharing on Central Counterparties (CCPs).

National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) Constitutes Advisory Panel on Audit Quality and Technology

  • Institutional Modernisation: The National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) constituted a high-level Advisory Committee on Audit Quality, Assurance, and Technology.
  • Mandate & Strategic Scope:
    • Formulate modern auditing standards, enhance supervisory audit inspection methodologies, and institutionalise AI and automated audit analytics tools to detect corporate misstatements.
    • Mandated under Section 132 of the Companies Act, 2013.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE

CAPITAL MARKETS & REGULATORY № 7

SEBI Introduces IT Resilience Index (ITRI) Framework for Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs)

  • Genesis & Systemic Risk Oversight: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) issued a master circular establishing an IT Resilience Index (ITRI) framework for Market Infrastructure Institutions (MIIs)—encompassing Stock Exchanges, Clearing Corporations, and Depositories—to continuously assess, audit, and benchmark systemic operational stability and disaster resilience.
  • The 100-Point Scoring Model Across 9 Parameters:
    • System Availability: 20% weightage (core transaction processing uptime, failover efficiency, and near-zero RPO/RTO).
    • Cybersecurity Posture: 20% weightage (threat detection capabilities, SOC defense, and perimeter vulnerability mitigation).
    • Data Integrity: 10% weightage (ledger consistency, transaction reconciliation, and tamper-resistance).
    • IT Governance: 10% weightage (board-level technology oversight, risk frameworks, and regulatory reporting).
    • Reliability & Performance Monitoring: 10% weightage (latency benchmarks, throughput stress testing, and real-time observability).
    • Business Continuity Planning (BCP) & Disaster Recovery (DR): 10% weightage (live DR drills and secondary data centre operational parity).
    • Modularity & Architecture Flexibility: 10% weightage (component decoupling, API resilience, and scalable middleware).
    • System Scalability: 5% weightage (peak trading volume headroom and capacity planning).
    • Incident Handling & Root Cause Analysis: 5% weightage (mean time to detect/resolve and statutory forensic disclosures).
  • Implementation Mechanism: The Industry Standards Forum (ISF), comprising technical leaders from MIIs, has been mandated to formulate standardized assessment metrics, automated data feeds, and quarterly self-assessment scorecards.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Institutional Coverage: Mandatory for all MIIs (Stock Exchanges, Clearing Corporations, and Depositories).
  • Dominant Weightage Parameters: Availability (20%) and Cybersecurity (20%) together constitute 40% of the aggregate index.
  • 5% Weightage Parameters: Scalability (5%) and Incident Handling (5%) (classic examiner trap).
  • Standard-Setting Body: Industry Standards Forum (ISF) in consultation with SEBI.

2. 🏦 BANKING, MONETARY POLICY & FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 8

Coastal Local Area Bank Admitted to Second Schedule of RBI Act, 1934: India's First Scheduled LAB

  • Historic Scheduled Status: The Reserve Bank of India officially accorded Scheduled Bank status to Coastal Local Area Bank Limited (Coastal LAB).
  • Inclusion in Second Schedule:
    • Coastal LAB becomes India's first Local Area Bank to be inscribed in the Second Schedule of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
    • Headquartered at Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh.
  • Prudential Liquidity & Operational Privileges:
    • Eligible to access RBI's liquidity windows, including the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF), repo auctions, and Marginal Standing Facility (MSF).
    • Authorized to participate in primary clearing houses, undertake government agency banking, and issue commercial certificates of deposit (CDs).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Institution: Coastal Local Area Bank (Coastal LAB).
  • Headquarters: Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh.
  • Milestone: First Local Area Bank (LAB) in India to receive Scheduled Bank status.
  • Statutory Inscription: Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934.
  • Target MCQ Form: "Which bank became India's first Local Area Bank (LAB) to be included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934 in September 2026?" → Coastal Local Area Bank.

RBI Launches Quarterly Monetary Policy Input Surveys: CCS, IESH, and Rural RCCS Battery

  • Statutory Forecasting Inputs: Ahead of the upcoming Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) bi-monthly review, the RBI rolled out its quarterly survey battery across 19 major cities and rural belts:
    1. Consumer Confidence Survey (CCS): Assesses urban household perceptions and 1-year expectations regarding general economic conditions, employment, prices, and spending.
    2. Inflation Expectations Survey of Households (IESH): Gauges qualitative and quantitative inflation projections over 3-month and 1-year horizons across 6,000+ urban households.
    3. Rural Consumer Confidence Survey (RCCS): Captures rural household economic confidence, agricultural wages, and discretionary consumption indices.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Three Anchor Surveys: CCS, IESH, and RCCS.
  • Primary Policy Destination: Acts as direct empirical input for the 6-member Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) benchmark rate determination.

    • Exempts this targeted equity acquisition from the aggregate regulatory ceiling on UCB investments in non-SLR securities and commercial equity, subject to specific capital adequacy safeguards.

RBI Approves LIC Stake Acquisition Up to 9.99% in ICICI Bank & Imposes ₹26.82 Lakh Fine on CIBIL

RBI Relaxes Concessional USD-INR Swap Access Norms & Appoints Suman Ray as Executive Director

  • Forex Swap Window Liberalisation: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) relaxed the access rules for its concessional USD-INR foreign exchange swap facility linked to Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) / FCNR(B) deposits.
  • The $100 Million Exemption Architecture:
    • Transactions Exceeding $100 Million: Authorised Dealer (AD) Category-I banks are now permitted to approach the RBI swap desk on any business day outside their predetermined weekly window, providing swift forex liquidity headroom during market volatility.
    • Transactions Up to $100 Million: Remain strictly governed by the bank's designated weekly operational day to ensure orderly central bank balance sheet management.
  • Central Banking Executive Leadership:
    • RBI appointed career central banker Suman Ray as Executive Director (ED) effective September 1, 2026 (elevated from Regional Director for Maharashtra).
    • Assigned Portfolios: Appointed to head the Department of DICGC (Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation) and the Premises Department.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Swap Access Threshold: Transactions above $100 Million can be executed on any business day (transactions ≤ $100M stay on weekly allocated day).
  • Underlying Anchor: Concessional forex swap facility linked to FCNR(B) deposits.
  • Suman Ray's Central Bank Portfolios: Department of DICGC and Premises Department.
  • Statutory Deposit Insurance Baseline: ₹5 Lakh per depositor per insured bank under the DICGC Act, 1961.
DISPATCH № 16

State Bank of India Revises BSBDA Branch Cash Withdrawal Fee Architecture Effective October 1, 2026

  • Regulatory Scope & Product Code: State Bank of India (SBI) issued a customer directive revising the cash withdrawal charge matrix for Basic Savings Bank Deposit Accounts (BSBDA) under Product Code 1011-1701, taking effect on October 1, 2026.
  • Revised Withdrawal Entitlements & Surcharges:
    • Free Branch Counter Allowance: Account holders are entitled to 4 free cash withdrawals per calendar month across SBI branch networks.
    • Beyond Monthly Limit: Every cash withdrawal beyond the 4 free transactions will attract a flat charge of ₹15 plus applicable GST (irrespective of the transaction amount withdrawn).
  • Absolute Exemption for Digital Channels:
    • SBI clarified that alternative banking channels—including UPI transactions, ATM cash withdrawals, and Net/Mobile Banking (NEFT/IMPS)—remain 100% free and do not count toward the 4-withdrawal monthly quota.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Effective Date: October 1, 2026.
  • Monthly Free Branch Transactions: 4 withdrawals.
  • Post-Limit Flat Fee: ₹15 + applicable GST per withdrawal.
  • Account Nomenclature: Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (Product Code 1011-1701).
  • Examiner's Trap: Surcharges apply strictly to branch cash counter withdrawals; digital payments (UPI/ATM) remain free.

INTERNATIONAL DIPLOMACY № 22

Bank of Baroda Unveils 'UPI Global Reverse Acceptance' for Inbound International Travellers

  • First-in-Market Cross-Border P2M Milestone: Bank of Baroda (BoB) launched “UPI Global Reverse Acceptance”, becoming the first public sector bank in India to operationalise inbound QR payments for foreign tourists, international business delegations, and Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) arriving in India.
  • Operational Architecture:
    • Allows visitors from countries participating in NPCI International's global partner network to make instant Person-to-Merchant (P2M) payments by scanning Bank of Baroda UPI QR codes at Indian merchants.
    • Foreign digital wallets or international bank apps are debited directly in foreign currency, while the Indian merchant instantly receives settlement in Indian Rupees (INR), eliminating physical currency conversion and point-of-sale foreign card markups.
  • Strategic Network Convergence: Directly integrated with NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL), expanding financial interconnectivity across India's merchant corridors.

  • Infrastructure Backing: NPCI International Payments Limited (NIPL).
  • Target MCQ Form: "Which Indian bank introduced 'UPI Global Reverse Acceptance' to facilitate inbound P2M payments for foreign tourists scanning Indian UPI QRs?" → Bank of Baroda.
INDICES & RATINGS № 23

NCDEX Launches 'RAINCHNNAI': India's First Weather Index Monsoon Futures Derivative

  • Pioneering Climate Derivative: The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX), regulated by SEBI, launched “RAINCHNNAI”, India's first weather index futures derivative contract, with trading commencing on August 31, 2026.
  • Hedging Chennai's Northeast Monsoon:
    • Designed to hedge financial, agricultural, and commercial risks associated with rainfall fluctuations during Chennai's Northeast monsoon (which accounts for approximately 70% of Chennai's 1,400 mm annual rainfall).
    • Monthly Contract Slate: Contracts are listed across 4 consecutive calendar months: September, October, November, and December.
  • Contract Mechanics & Index Pricing:
    • Pricing Engine: Constructed on a Cumulative Deviation Rainfall (CDR) index model based on official IMD automated weather station observations.
    • Tick Size & Lot Constraints: Minimum tick size of 1 millimetre; maximum single order lot size restricted to 50 lots.
    • Settlement: Strictly cash-settled against cumulative precipitation deviations; trading runs Monday through Friday between 10:00 AM and 11:30 PM / 11:55 PM.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Exchange: NCDEX (National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange; HQ: Mumbai).
  • Specific Meteorological Target: Northeast Monsoon (retreating monsoon affecting Tamil Nadu).
  • Index Model: Cumulative Deviation Rainfall (CDR) model.
  • Contract Parameters: 1 mm tick size, max 50 lots, strictly cash-settled.
  • Examiner's Trap: Setting the question as Southwest Monsoon or claim physical commodity delivery—it is cash-settled on precipitation index deviation.

Paatil, the Chief Ministers of Bihar and Jharkhand executed a landmark bilateral agreement resolving the 25-year-old water-sharing dispute over the Sone River basin originating from the Bihar Reorganisation Act, 2000.

    • Jharkhand's Allocation: Awarded 2.00 Million Acre-Feet (MAF), providing guaranteed industrial, municipal, and irrigation supply for drought-prone Palamu and Garhwa districts as well as North Karanpura industrial corridors.
  • Key Strategic Reservoirs on Sone Basin:

DISPATCH № 36

Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules 2026 Notified & National Tribunals Data Grid Enacted

  • Statutory Mandate for IST: The Department of Consumer Affairs (DoCA), Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, notified the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026 under Section 52 of the Legal Metrology Act, 2009.
  • 'One Nation, One Time' Operational Directives:
    • Establishes Indian Standard Time (IST) as the single, uniform legal reference for all administrative, commercial, financial, and legal actions across India, coming into force 180 days after Gazette publication.
    • Clocks in critical national infrastructure—including banking, digital payments, telecom switches, power grids, and stock exchanges—must synchronise via Network Time Protocol (NTP) and Precision Time Protocol (PTP).
    • Scientific Custodian: IST (UTC+05:30 based on 82.5°E longitude) is generated and maintained solely by the CSIR-National Physical Laboratory (CSIR-NPL) in New Delhi (not IMD or ISRO), utilizing NavIC satellite signals and White Rabbit precision optical timing.
  • National Tribunals Reforms Bill 2026:
    • Repeals the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 and mandates the development of the National Tribunals Data Grid (NTDG)—a unified portal tracking cases across 16 tribunals (over 5.24 lakh pending cases).
    • Governed by the National Tribunals Commission (NTC): Comprises a Chairperson (retired SC Judge or HC Chief Justice), 2 Judicial Members, and 2 Technical Members (minimum 25 years' professional experience in finance, law, or tech; 5-year tenure or up to age 70).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Legal Mandate: Section 52, Legal Metrology Act, 2009 (Implementation window: 180 days).
  • Sole Custodian of IST: CSIR-National Physical Laboratory (CSIR-NPL) (common examiner trap: IMD or ISRO).
  • Synchronisation Technologies: NavIC, NTP, PTP, and White Rabbit protocol.
  • NTDG Institutional Framework: 16 tribunals under National Tribunals Commission (age ceiling: 70 years).

AVNL Jabalpur T-72 & T-90 Tank Overhaul Facility (₹472 Cr) & GE Aerospace Delivers 3 F404 Engines to HAL

  • National Main Battle Tank Overhaul Architecture:

1. 🏛️ RBI POLICY, MASTER DIRECTIONS & PRUDENTIAL NORMS

MONETARY POLICY COMMITTEE № 1

Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) — Benchmark Rate Corridor Trajectory

  • Continuous Policy Rate Pause: The MPC held the Policy Repo Rate at 5.25% with a neutral monetary stance across four consecutive bi-monthly reviews through the August 3–5, 2026 meeting (next review scheduled for Oct 5–7, 2026).
  • Standing Facility Rate Structure: Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) fixed at 5.00% (Repo - 25 bps); Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) and Bank Rate fixed at 5.50% (Repo + 25 bps); Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) holds at 3.00%; Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) holds at 18.00%.
  • Statutory MPC Composition: 6-member committee under Section 45-ZB of the RBI Act, 1934; comprises 3 RBI officials (Governor Sanjay Malhotra as Chairperson, Deputy Governor, Executive Director) and 3 external government-appointed experts.
  • Live Macroeconomic Projections: MPC revised India's FY27 real GDP growth projection up to 6.7% (from 6.6%), while trimming FY27 CPI inflation projection down to 5.0% (from 5.1%).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Corridor Math: Repo = 5.25%, SDF = 5.00%, MSF/Bank Rate = 5.50% (SDF is always 25 bps below Repo; MSF is 25 bps above).
  • Stance Confusion: Monetary stance is NEUTRAL (not 'Withdrawal of Accommodation').
  • Target MCQ Form: "What is the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate following RBI's August 2026 Monetary Policy Committee review?" → 5.00%.
DISPATCH № 2

Digital Fraud Compensation: Responsible Business Conduct (Third Amendment) Directions

  • Genesis & Compensation Slabs: Framed to protect victims of small-value, unauthorized electronic banking transactions (losses up to ₹50,000); mandates compensation of 85% of net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is lower.
  • Institutional Loss-Apportionment Formula: For losses below ₹29,412, the 85% payout is apportioned: RBI bears 65% (funded via Depositor Education and Awareness / DEA Fund), the customer's issuing bank bears 10%, and the beneficiary bank bears 10%.
  • Statutory Deferred Effective Date: Formally notified in the Gazette on June 24, 2026, but RBI deferred enforcement to January 1, 2027 (pushed from the original July 1, 2026 draft date) to give banks integration runway.
  • Zero Customer Liability Principle: Guarantees zero liability where digital fraud occurs due to bank negligence or third-party breaches reported by the customer within 3 working days.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • The Date Trap: Implementation date is January 1, 2027 (do NOT pick July 1, 2026).
  • The Cap Trap: Compensation is 85% of loss or ₹25,000, whichever is LOWER (not ₹50,000).
  • Target MCQ Form: "Under the RBI Responsible Business Conduct Directions, what is the mandatory effective date for the small-value digital fraud compensation framework?" → January 1, 2027.
DISPATCH № 3

Bank Dividend Payout Cap Overhaul: Graded CET1 Capital Architecture

  • Dismantling Legacy Cap: RBI dismantled the rigid decades-old regulation that strictly capped commercial bank dividend distributions at a uniform 40% of Profit After Tax (PAT).
  • Graded Capital-Linked Ceiling: Operational from FY26 balance sheets, maximum dividend payout is raised up to 75% of PAT for commercial banks maintaining a Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio ≥ 13.0%.
  • Foreign Bank Branch Remittances: Foreign banks operating in India via branch mode are permitted to remit up to 80% of net post-tax profits to head offices abroad, provided local Capital Conservation Buffers are met.
  • Asset Quality Barrier: A bank is statutorily disqualified from declaring dividends if its Net Non-Performing Assets (NNPA) ratio exceeds 6.0% for the financial year.

Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework for Commercial Banks & NBFCs

  • Three Mandatory Risk Threshold Parameters: RBI monitors regulated financial institutions across three diagnostic financial metrics: (1) Capital (CRAR & CET1), (2) Asset Quality (Net NPA ratio), and (3) Leverage (Tier-1 Leverage Ratio).
  • Breach Threshold Slabs:
    • Risk Threshold 1: Triggered if Net NPA exceeds 6.0% (mandatory restriction on dividend payout and profit repatriation).
    • Risk Threshold 2: Triggered if Net NPA exceeds 9.0% (mandatory restriction on branch expansion).
    • Risk Threshold 3: Triggered if Net NPA exceeds 12.0% (mandatory restriction on capital expenditure and management compensation).
  • NBFC Inclusion: Extended to Middle, Upper, and Top-Layer NBFCs under Scale-Based Regulation to prevent systemic shadow-banking defaults.

  • Threshold 1 Net NPA: Threshold 1 is breached at 6.0% Net NPA.

  • Four-Layer Regulatory Architecture:

    • Middle Layer (NBFC-ML): Assets ≥ ₹1,000 crore
    • Upper Layer (NBFC-UL): Top 25 identified systemic entities or assets ≥ ₹1 lakh crore
    • Top Layer (NBFC-TL): Activated only under extreme contagion risk (currently empty)

INTERNATIONAL DIPLOMACY № 37

UPI CIRCLE № 39

UPI Circle — Delegated Payments Architecture for Family Accounts

  • Secondary User Authorization: NPCI launched 'UPI Circle', enabling a primary bank account holder to authorize a trusted secondary user (family member, dependent, child) to execute payments from the primary account.
  • Two Delegation Modalities:
    • Full Delegation: Primary user establishes a monthly spending cap (maximum ₹15,000 per month), allowing the secondary user to spend autonomously within limits without secondary approval.
    • Partial Delegation: Secondary user initiates the payment request, but each transaction requires final biometric or PIN authorization from the primary user.
  • Security Guardrails: Primary user can link a maximum of 5 secondary delegates and revoke authorization in real time.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Monthly Cap: Under Full Delegation, the maximum monthly spending limit set by the primary user is ₹15,000 (not ₹25,000).
  • Delegate Count: A primary user can authorize up to 5 secondary delegates.
  • Target MCQ Form: "What is the maximum monthly transaction limit permissible under the 'Full Delegation' mode of NPCI's UPI Circle?" → ₹15,000.
CENTRAL BANK DIGITAL CURRENCY № 40

Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) — Sovereign e-Rupee Innovations

  • Dual Pilot Architecture: RBI operates two distinct pilots: e₹-W (Wholesale) launched Nov 1, 2022 (interbank settlement of secondary G-sec transactions and call money market) and e₹-R (Retail) launched Dec 1, 2022.
  • Programmability & Offline Capabilities: Enabled programmable e-Rupee tokens with targeted end-use (e.g., direct benefit transfer for agricultural input subsidies, school fee vouchers) with automated expiry dates and merchant geofencing.
  • UPI Interoperability: e₹-R wallets can scan any standard interoperable UPI QR code, enabling consumers to spend digital rupees at over 30 million merchant touchpoints nationwide.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Wholesale vs Retail Dates: Wholesale pilot was launched on Nov 1, 2022; Retail pilot launched on Dec 1, 2022.
  • Interest Bearing: The sovereign CBDC (e-Rupee) is non-interest bearing by law to prevent disintermediation of commercial bank deposits.

Card-on-File Tokenisation (CoFT) via Card-Issuing Banks

  • Tokenisation Transition: Prohibits merchants, payment aggregators, and payment gateways from storing actual customer card details (16-digit PAN, CVV, expiry date); mandates replacement with unique cryptographic tokens.
  • Direct CoFT Enablement: RBI permitted cardholders to create and view tokens directly through mobile banking and internet banking portals of their card-issuing banks, eliminating dependence on merchant check-out pages.
  • Alternate Authentication Mechanisms (AAM): RBI issued draft directions allowing banks to deploy non-SMS factor-of-authentication mechanisms, such as in-app biometric approvals, behavioral risk scoring, and hardware tokens.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE

MACRO • FISCAL & TAX № 53

Fiscal Deficit Consolidation & The Sovereign Debt Glide Path

  • Annual Deficit Target: Revised fiscal deficit for FY25 estimated at 4.9% of GDP (improved from interim target of 5.1%); projected to compress below 4.5% of GDP in FY26.
  • Post-FY26 Fiscal Anchor: Shifting away from an absolute fiscal deficit percentage towards a debt-to-GDP reduction anchor, aiming to lower central government debt from ~56% of GDP towards sustainable multi-year thresholds.

Capital Gains Taxation Architecture: Dual Rationalization

  • Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG): STCG on specified financial assets (listed equities and equity-oriented mutual funds covered under Section 111A) hiked from 15% to 20%.
  • Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG):

    • Annual exemption limit for LTCG on equity assets increased from ₹1 Lakh to ₹1.25 Lakh.
  • Holding Period Standardization: Simplified into two holding periods across all asset classes: 12 months for all listed securities; 24 months for all unlisted securities and real estate.

  • Historic Startup Relief: Completely abolished the 'Angel Tax' for all classes of investors across all registered startup companies with immediate effect.

INDICES & RATINGS № 62

Wholesale Price Index (WPI) & Consumer Price Index (CPI) Structural Anchors

  • Base Year Parameters:
    • Consumer Price Index (CPI - Combined): Base Year is 2012=100; published monthly by the National Statistical Office (NSO), MoSPI.
    • Wholesale Price Index (WPI): Base Year is 2011-12=100; published monthly by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
  • Weightage Distribution Traps:
    • CPI Weights: Food & Beverages = 45.86%; Housing = 10.07% (urban only); Fuel & Light = 6.84%; Miscellaneous = 28.32%.
    • WPI Weights: Manufactured Products = 64.23%; Primary Articles = 22.62%; Fuel & Power = 13.15% (Note: Services are completely excluded from WPI).
  • Inflation Targeting Metric: Under Section 45-ZA of the RBI Act, the official inflation target of 4% (±2% tolerance band) is legally bound to CPI-Combined, NOT WPI.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Official Anchor: Monetary policy inflation targeting legally uses CPI-Combined (2012=100), NEVER WPI.
  • WPI Heavyweight: Largest component of WPI is Manufactured Products (64.23%); Food in CPI is 45.86%.
  • Target MCQ Form: "Which inflation index serves as the statutory nominal anchor for the Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee?" → Consumer Price Index (CPI - Combined).

  • Dual Corridor Architecture:

    • Northern Corridor: Connecting Arabian Gulf ports via high-speed railway networks through UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan to Israeli port of Haifa, and onward to European ports (Piraeus, Greece).
  • Strategic Triad Infrastructure: Beyond freight rail and shipping lanes, IMEC integrates an electricity cable grid, a high-capacity clean hydrogen export pipeline, and high-speed digital fiber-optic cables.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Founding Forum: Launched during the G20 New Delhi Leaders' Summit (September 2023).
  • Non-Signatories: Neither China nor Turkey are signatories to the IMEC pact.
  • Target MCQ Form: "On the sidelines of which international summit was the historic India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) MoU signed?" → G20 New Delhi Summit.
DISPATCH № 102

India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA)

  • Historic European Free Trade Accord: Signed between India and the 4-nation European Free Trade Association (EFTA) comprising Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, and Liechtenstein.
  • First-of-its-Kind $100 Billion Investment Commitment: EFTA nations committed legally to invest $100 Billion in India over 15 years (generating over 1 million direct jobs) as a reciprocal condition for tariff concessions.
  • Tariff Phase-Out Scope: India provided tariff concessions on 82.7% of its tariff lines covering Swiss watches, machinery, precision instruments, and chocolates (excluding domestic agriculture and dairy sectors).

DISPATCH № 103

India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA) & LCS

  • Local Currency Settlement (LCS) System: Operationalized direct bilateral trade settlement in Indian Rupee (INR) and UAE Dirham (AED), bypassing USD intermediation.
  • Payment Linkages: Integrated India's UPI with UAE's Aani/Jaywan instant payment system and linked national card switches (RuPay and Jaywan).
  • Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT): Formally signed the India-UAE Bilateral Investment Treaty in Abu Dhabi, replacing the older Bilateral Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (BIPPA).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • UAE Domestic Card System: UAE's sovereign domestic card switch linked with RuPay is Jaywan.
  • Currencies: Bilateral trade settled directly in INR and AED.
  • Target MCQ Form: "Which domestic payment card network of the UAE has been integrated with India's RuPay network?" → Jaywan.

8. ⚖️ REGULATORY BODIES, ACTS, COMMITTEES & APPOINTMENTS

DISPATCH № 106

Telecommunications Act, 2023 Enacted into Law

  • Century-Old Law Repeal: Formally repealed archaic colonial legislations: the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, and the Telegraph Wires (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1950.
  • Administrative Allocation of Satellite Spectrum: Mandated the administrative allocation of satellite communication spectrum (satcom) without competitive auctioning, aligning India with global ITU standards for Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb, and Jio Satellite.
  • Digital Bharat Nidhi: Renamed and restructured the Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) into 'Digital Bharat Nidhi' to support R&D, pilot deployment, and rural broadband expansion.
  • Biometric SIM Guardrails: Enforces mandatory biometric verification for SIM acquisition, prescribing penalties up to ₹50 Lakh and 3 years imprisonment for fraudulent acquisition using forged identities.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Satellite Spectrum Allocation: Allocated ADMINISTRATIVELY, not through public auction.
  • Renamed USOF: USOF was renamed to Digital Bharat Nidhi.
  • Target MCQ Form: "Under the Telecommunications Act 2023, the Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) was renamed as which entity?" → Digital Bharat Nidhi.
DISPATCH № 107

Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 Regulatory Framework

  • Statutory Genesis & DPBI: Establishes the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI) as an autonomous digital adjudicatory authority to investigate breaches and impose statutory penalties.
  • Penalties Slabs:
    • Failure to prevent significant personal data breach: Penalties up to ₹250 Crore.
    • Failure to fulfill duties of Data Fiduciary towards children: Up to ₹200 Crore.
    • General non-compliance penalties: Up to ₹50 Crore.
  • Consent Architecture: Introduces the legal concept of 'Consent Managers' registered with the DPBI, interoperable consent withdrawal, and mandatory notice in all 22 Eighth Schedule languages.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Maximum Penalty: Maximum penalty for failing to prevent a significant data breach is ₹250 Crore per instance.
  • Adjudicating Body: Governed by the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI).
  • Target MCQ Form: "What is the maximum financial penalty that can be imposed under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 for failure to prevent a personal data breach?" → ₹250 Crore.
DISPATCH № 108

Criminal Justice Overhaul: BNS, BNSS & BSA Operationalization

  • Enforcement Date: Came into full legal effect across India on July 1, 2024, completely replacing the British-era penal codes.
  • Three Replaced Statutes:
    1. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.
    2. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.
    3. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
  • Pioneering Legal Reforms:
    • Introduction of Zero FIR (can be registered at any police station regardless of jurisdiction).
    • Mandatory audio-video recording of search and seizure operations.
    • Introduction of Community Service as a recognized punishment for petty offenses.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Enforcement Date: Enacted into law on July 1, 2024 (not Jan 1 or April 1).
  • Law Mapping: BNS = IPC; BNSS = CrPC; BSA = Evidence Act.
  • Target MCQ Form: "On which date did the three new criminal laws (BNS, BNSS, and BSA) come into legal force across India?" → July 1, 2024.

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 5

RBI draft/proposed frameworks — consolidated tracker

  • A) Interest Rates on Loans and Advances Directions, 2026 (draft, eff. 1 April 2027): rate linked to benchmark + risk-based spread; floating reset ≤ once/3 months; agri loans reset ≤12 months tied to crop season; external benchmark mandatory for floating personal/MSME loans.
  • B) On-tap UCB licences: large credit coops (≥10 yrs, ≥₹10,000 cr deposits, ≥₹300 cr net worth, CRAR ≥12%, NNPA ≤3%) can convert; Phase 1 = Multi-State Coop Societies Act 2002 entities only; 5% shareholding cap.
  • C) Recovery-agent norms: eff. 1 Jan 2027; contact only 8 AM–7 PM; India's first phone-lock-restriction framework — no restriction before 30 days overdue, full restriction after 60 days; device restored within 1 hr of payment or ₹250/hr penalty.
  • D) CVA derivative-risk framework (proposed eff. 1 April 2027): simplified approach for banks with non-centrally-cleared derivatives ≤₹10 trillion.
  • E) Leverage ratio buffer for G-SIB branches (proposed eff. 1 April 2027): min leverage 4% (D-SIBs)/3.5% (others). Current D-SIBs: SBI (+0.80% CET1), HDFC Bank (+0.40%), ICICI Bank (+0.20%).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE Don't confuse the three 2027 dates: recovery norms (1 Jan 2027) vs CVA & leverage buffer (both 1 April 2027, different rules).

POLICY & STRATEGIC ACCORDS № 12

GOBARdhan: Fuelling Clean Energy and Rural Growth — full scheme detail 🔄 UPDATE (PIB 1–10 Aug backgrounder, merged with the entry above)

  • Full form: Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan; approved by Union Cabinet 6 August 2026; Nodal Ministry MoPNG; originally launched 2018 under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), Solid & Liquid Waste Management component
  • Core concept: converts cattle dung, agri residue, press mud, municipal/kitchen/market organic waste into Compressed Biogas (CBG) — chemically equivalent to natural gas — and organic manure
  • Six Growth Engines: (1) Assured CBG Offtake — CGD entities procure under a notified CBG Obligation trajectory: 3% FY 2026-27 → 4% FY 2027-28 → 5% from FY 2028-29 onwards in CNG (Transport)/PNG (Domestic) segments; (2) Stable Pricing — administered price ₹2,110/MMBTU (~₹105/kg); (3) Capital Assistance — up to ₹2 crore/TPD of installed CBG capacity for greenfield projects; (4) Pipeline Infrastructure — connects CBG plants to trunk pipelines & CGD networks; (5) Credit Guarantee — up to 85% coverage for eligible MSME-based CBG projects; (6) CBG Ecosystem Challenge Fund — feedstock mapping, aggregation, tech, district planning, manure value addition
  • Supporting initiatives: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation — promotes CBG production/supply to OMCs); Biomass Aggregation Machinery (BAM) Scheme — outlay ₹564.75 crore; Development of Pipeline Infrastructure (DPI) Scheme — outlay ₹994.5 crore, FY24-25 to FY28-29; MDA Scheme — Market Development Assistance for organic manure, ₹1,500/MT; CFA — Central Financial Assistance for CBG plants under National Bioenergy Programme
  • GOBARdhan Unified Registration Portal — registration required to avail MoPNG benefits/support
  • Top-performing states: 1. Uttar Pradesh → 2. Madhya Pradesh → 3. Maharashtra → 4. Gujarat → 5. Telangana; Top banks: 1. SBI → 2. BoB → 3. Union Bank of India → 4. PNB → 5. Indian Bank; Top ULB: Municipal Corporation of Delhi
  • 2026-36 expected outcomes: CBG 10×, fossil-fuel displacement 10 MMT, forex savings >₹40,000 cr, GDP addition >₹75,000 cr, >1.5 lakh jobs, CO₂ reduction >40 MT, organic fertilizer 250 MMT
🎯 EXAM ANGLE Six Growth Engines' CBG Obligation trajectory (3%→4%→5%) is a strong sequencing trap alongside the already-known ₹23,731 cr outlay; don't confuse GOBARdhan's original 2018 launch (under Swachh Bharat) with its 6 Aug 2026 Cabinet-approved revamp.

PRADHAN MANTRI ANNADATA AAY SA... № 48

Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-AASHA) — Revamped Architecture (PIB 21–22 Aug)

🪝 An integrated umbrella scheme to protect farmgate prices through 4 distinct mechanisms with a ₹7,200 crore budget allocation for FY 2026–27.

  • Launch & Mandate: September 2018; comprehensive MSP assurance framework.
  • Four Distinct Components:
    1. Price Support Scheme (PSS): Physical procurement of pulses, oilseeds, and copra at MSP through NAFED and NCCF. Procurement limit: Initially up to 25% of State/UT production (can be raised up to 25% of national production). Exception: For Tur, Urad, and Masur, procurement is permitted up to 100% of State production.
    2. Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS): Direct cash transfer of price difference between MSP and market price (up to 15% of MSP value); no physical procurement; primarily applied to oilseeds.
    3. Price Stabilization Fund (PSF): Maintained by Department of Consumer Affairs for strategic buffer stocking of essential food items (pulses, onion, potato) to curb consumer retail spikes; now formally integrated under PM-AASHA.
    4. Market Intervention Scheme (MIS): Applied to perishable horticultural commodities (e.g., Tomato, Onion, Potato - TOP) lacking formal MSP; activated when market price crashes by ≥10% below previous normal season rate.
  • Budget Allocation (2026–27): ₹7,200 crore.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE Don't confuse PDPS (max 15% price difference, zero procurement) with PSS (physical procurement up to 25%, but 100% for Tur/Urad/Masur); MIS trigger threshold is a 10% price fall.

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 54

RBI Fair Practices Code & Directives on Loan Recovery & Recovery Agents

  • Scope & Applicability: Issued to all Regulated Entities (REs) including Commercial Banks, All-India Financial Institutions (AIFIs), NBFCs, and Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks.
  • Strict Calling Hours Window: Recovery agents and bank staff are strictly permitted to contact borrowers only between 8:00 AM and 7:00 PM. Any call, visit, or digital communication before 8 AM or after 7 PM is legally prohibited.
  • Prohibited Conduct & Anti-Harassment Mandate: • Zero tolerance for threatening, abusive, or humiliating language towards borrowers or their guarantors. • Strict ban on public humiliation, making unsolicited persistent calls, contacting family members/friends, or intruding on privacy. • REs cannot forward recovery calls through hidden numbers or masked spoofed caller IDs.
  • Agent Due Diligence & Certification: Mandatory police background verification prior to engagement; recovery agents must possess valid IIBF Debt Recovery Agent (DRA) certification and undergo structured training on code of conduct.
  • Sole Accountability: The Regulated Entity remains solely liable for all actions, misconduct, and transgressions of recovery agents engaged directly or via third-party agencies.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Calling Hours Trap: Permitted window is 8:00 AM to 7:00 PM (examiners often trap with 7 AM–9 PM or 9 AM–6 PM).
  • Mandatory Certification: Must hold Indian Institute of Banking & Finance (IIBF) DRA certificate.
  • Entity Liability: Outsourcing recovery does NOT transfer liability; REs face direct penal action for agent harassment.
DISPATCH № 55

Basel III Additional Tier-1 (AT-1) Bonds & Regulatory Safeguards

  • Capital Classification: Issued as unsecured, perpetual, subordinated debt instruments to meet Tier-1 capital requirements under RBI Basel III norms.
  • Trigger Level & Loss Absorption: Feature a pre-specified contractual trigger: if a bank's Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) drops below 5.5% (or at the Point of Non-Viability - PONV), AT-1 bonds face mandatory permanent write-down or equity conversion.
  • Call Option Regulations: Minimum maturity is perpetual; call options can only be exercised after a minimum of 5 years with prior approval of the RBI.
  • Retail Investor Protection: Retail individual investors cannot be directly allotted AT-1 bonds; minimum ticket size on private placement is set at ₹1 crore.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Loss Absorption Trigger: CET1 breaching below 5.5% triggers automatic write-off/conversion.
  • Call Option Restriction: Minimum 5 years (cannot have a put option for investors).
  • Allotment Floor: Minimum ticket size ₹1 crore to restrict vulnerable retail participation.

POLICY & STRATEGIC ACCORDS № 74

Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026 — National Tribunals Commission (NTC) full composition 🔄 UPDATE (PIB 11–18 Aug backgrounder, merged with the NTDG entry above)

  • Passed by Parliament in August 2026 to make tribunals independent, transparent, efficient & uniform; repeals Tribunal Reforms Act, 2021; basis — SC directions in Madras Bar Association v. Union of India
  • NTC Composition: Chairperson (SC Judge/HC Chief Justice); Four Members — 2 Judicial Members (HC Chief Justice/HC Judge) + 2 Technical Members (25+ years' experience in public administration, finance, law, accountancy, banking, management or technology); appointment by Central Govt, after consultation with CJI for Chairperson & Judicial Members
  • NTC's 4 major functions: Selection, Review performance (monitor tribunals + annual reports), Inquiries, Data (→ National Tribunals Data Grid, covering the already-noted 16 tribunals)
  • Tenure: NTC Chairperson/Members — 5 years/age 70, whichever earlier; Tribunal Members — 5 years/age 67, whichever earlier; reappointment allowed based on previous service & performance
  • Search-cum-Selection Committees: for Chairperson selection — Committee Chair is the NTC Chairperson, plus 1 Technical Member, a retired HC Chief Justice, a GoI Secretary/State Chief Secretary (for SATs), 2 empanelled experts, and a Member Secretary; for Member selection — Committee Chair is the NTC Judicial Member, with an analogous composition (retired HC Judge instead of retired Chief Justice)
  • Key provisions: Committee Chair holds the casting vote; Member Secretary + 2 expert members have no voting rights; recommendation = 1 suitable candidate/vacancy + 1 for waiting list; Timeline — Secretariat must communicate recommendations to Central Govt within 3 days; Government must process and appoint within 3 months
🎯 EXAM ANGLE NTC's 2 Judicial + 2 Technical Member composition and the 3-day/3-month appointment timeline is a strong new-body MCQ, layering onto the already-logged NTDG (16 tribunals) fact.

Samudra Manthan — National Offshore Exploration Scheme (PIB 1–10 Aug — standing exception, Template A regardless of zone)

🪝 Nearly all of India's previously "No-Go" offshore areas are now open for exploration under India's most ambitious offshore-oil mission yet.

  • Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan (India's most ambitious offshore exploration mission); Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas; Central Sector Scheme; Outlay ₹84,084 crore; Implementation up to FY 2030-31/31 March 2031; aim — reduce import dependence (India is world's 3rd-largest crude oil consumer), boost domestic O&G production
  • Components: Offshore seismic data acquisition & processing ₹28,534 cr; Accelerated deepwater exploration (60 wells) ₹43,200 cr; Common offshore infra hubs ₹10,000 cr; O&G Mfg/Services Zones + monitoring/support ₹2,350 cr (₹2,000 cr + ₹350 cr)
  • Govt support for deepwater drilling: up to 50% of eligible drilling cost or ₹675 crore/well, whichever is lower; focus basins — Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery, Mahanadi, Andaman; ~99% of previously restricted "No-Go" areas in India's EEZ opened for exploration
  • Key targets: domestic O&G production to 80 MMTOE annually; hydrocarbon resource base expansion to 2.2 billion TOE; potential crude-import reduction ~₹1 lakh crore annually

  • Objective: promote first-time employment, formal jobs, expand social security; announced August 2025; implementation 1 Aug 2025 – 31 July 2027 (2 years); outlay ₹99,446 crore; target >3.5 crore employment opportunities incl. 1.92 crore first-time employees; EPFO-linked digital platform; complements the National Manufacturing Mission

  • Part B (Employers): incentive up to ₹3,000/month per eligible additional employee, for 2 years (extended to 3rd/4th years for manufacturing sector)

MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 passed by Parliament (PIB 1–10 Aug)

  • Udyam-registered MSMEs: 9.16 crore; employment: 40+ crore people; focus — Ease of Doing Business, decriminalisation, formalisation, delayed-payment resolution
  • Makes Udyam Portal a permanent digital, free & voluntary registration platform
  • Court proceedings: mandates courts to order payment of at least 50% of the awarded amount to micro/small-enterprise suppliers if a set-aside application is pending 6+ months
  • Mediation to complete within 90 days of first appearance; arbitration reference within 30 days of mediation termination; arbitral award within 90 days of completion of pleadings
  • Recovery of dues (mediated settlement/arbitral award) recoverable as an "arrear of land revenue" via District Collector/Deputy Commissioner
  • TReDS: CPSEs mandated to route invoice settlements through it; invoice discounting rose to ₹3.47 lakh crore (2025-26)
  • States can establish multiple Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Councils (MSEFCs) and frame their own rules
  • Penalties: decriminalisation — conviction-based fines replaced by graded civil penalties

E-SAMUDRA, 5 YEARS OF E-SHRAM ... № 128

e-Samudra, 5 Years of e-Shram Portal & PM-SYM cluster 🔄 UPDATE (PIB 25–26 Aug)

  • e-Samudra — single-window digital maritime-governance platform, launched 8 August 2026 by Sarbananda Sonowal (Union Minister for Ports, Shipping & Waterways), Mumbai; shifts maritime administration to "Digital First and Faceless Governance"; incorporates e-NAVIK 24×7 grievance redressal, upcoming Seafarer Tracking Dashboard, Digital Seafarers Employment Agreement (d-SEA), enhanced Seafarers Welfare Fund Society (SWFS) measures.
  • 5 Years of e-Shram Portal (2021–2026):
    • Launched 26 August 2021 by Ministry of Labour & Employment, developed by NIC; India's first Aadhaar-authenticated National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW).
    • Every registered worker receives a unique permanent 12-digit Universal Account Number (UAN).
    • Registrations: 31.89 crore (as of 18 Aug 2026); 54.28% women vs 45.72% men; 55.21% aged 18–40 years; ~11.5 lakh gig and platform workers. Top states: UP, Bihar, West Bengal, MP, Maharashtra.
    • One-Stop Solution (launched 21 Oct 2024): Integrates 15 Social Security & Welfare Schemes (PM-SYM, PM-SBY, PM-JJBY, NCS, Skill India Digital Hub, BOCW); supports 22 scheduled languages via BHASHINI.
  • Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) — launched February 2019, Ministry of Labour & Employment; voluntary/contributory pension for unorganised-sector workers; assured pension ₹3,000/month after 60; eligibility — age 18-40, monthly income ≤₹15,000, not an EPFO/ESIC/NPS member or income-tax assessee; monthly contribution ₹55-₹200 (50% beneficiary + 50% Central Govt match); enrolment via Common Service Centres or maandhan.in; 54 lakh+ beneficiaries enrolled (29 July 2026), 53.1% women, Govt's matching contribution ₹2,011.01 crore; pension disbursement begins not before February 2039.

INTERNATIONAL DIPLOMACY № 129

India's Makhana Sector — Traditional Crop to Global Superfood (PIB 19 Aug Backgrounder)

🪝 Bihar accounts for 80–85% of global makhana supply, backed by a dedicated Central Sector Scheme and National Board.

  • Botanical Identity: Makhana (Euryale ferox), also known as fox nut or gorgon nut, aquatic crop grown in shallow wetlands.
  • Geographical Dominance: India is the world's leading producer; Bihar accounts for ~75% of India's production and 80–85% of global supply (Kosi basin: Supaul, Saharsa, Madhepura; Mithila and Seemanchal regions). 'Mithila Makhana' holds a registered GI Tag.
  • Institutional & Scheme Framework:
    • National Makhana Board: Announced in Union Budget 2025–26, formally launched in Bihar on 15 September 2025.
    • Central Sector Scheme for Development of Makhana: Outlay ₹476.03 crore (FY 2025–26 to FY 2030–31); allocations: ₹30 cr (FY26), ₹90 cr (FY27).
  • Production & Market Stats:
    • Production (2025–26 2nd AE): 80,590 MT (productivity 2.34 MT/ha); Bihar produces 60,000 MT. Improved varieties: Swarna Vaidehi and Sabour Makhana-1.
    • Domestic Market: Growing at 17–18% CAGR, projected to reach ₹11,000–12,000 crore by 2029–30.
    • Exports: India exports ~40% of production (~0.25 lakh MT). In 2025–26, exports were 7,264.89 MT (₹192.96 crore). USA (40%) > Canada > UAE account for 77% of total exports. Premium markets: Germany (26/kg),Nepal(26/kg), Nepal (26/kg),Nepal(21.6/kg), Australia ($21/kg).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE ₹476.03 crore Central Sector Scheme outlay; Bihar's 80–85% global dominance; USA as top export destination (40%).
NATIONAL ANIMAL DISEASE CONTRO... № 130

National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP) & Dairy Productivity (PIB 21–22 Aug Backgrounder)

  • Mission Mandate: 100% central programme under Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP, Budget FY27: ₹2,010 crore); launched September 2019 to eradicate Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) and Brucellosis by 2030.
  • Vaccination Strategy:
    • FMD: 100% vaccination of susceptible livestock twice a year (every 6 months); cumulative 147.16 crore doses.
    • Brucellosis: One-time lifetime vaccination for female bovine calves aged 4–8 months.
    • Vaccinator Remuneration: Minimum ₹3 per vaccination dose.
  • Digital Animal Stack: Bharat Pashudhan Portal — assigns a unique 12-digit Tag ID to every bovine; >39 crore livestock registered by July 2026; 4,019 Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) deployed.
  • Dairy Production & Productivity:
    • Annual milk production reached 247.87 million tonnes in 2024–25 (+69.4% decadal growth).
    • Bovine productivity rose to 2,250 kg/animal/year; target is 3,000 kg/animal/year by 2030.
  • Global Linkage: US$25 million Pandemic Fund project supported by G20 with ADB, FAO, and World Bank.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE FMD (every 6 months) vs Brucellosis (one-time lifetime at 4–8 months female calves); unique 12-digit Tag ID on Bharat Pashudhan; 3,000 kg/animal bovine productivity target by 2030.

    • Supporting Schemes: PKVY (₹31,500/ha over 3 yrs, 16.90 lakh ha); PDMC (55% subsidy for small/marginal, ₹26,325 cr released); Soil Health Card (12 parameters, 25.89 crore cards generated).

    • MSP notified for 87 Minor Forest Produce (MFP) items, procured via TRIFED and state agencies.

Cabinet Rationalization of Agriculture Schemes: PM-RKVY & Krishonnati Yojana (₹1.01 Lakh Cr Outlay)

  • Structural Consolidation: Union Cabinet approved the restructuring and consolidation of all centrally sponsored agricultural schemes under two simplified umbrella frameworks to eliminate overlap and enhance state flexibility:
    1. Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY): Focuses on sustainable agriculture, soil health, crop diversification, organic farming, and customized state agricultural project plans.
    2. Krishonnati Yojana (KY): Focuses on food security, technological self-reliance, horticulture missions, oilseeds/oil palm missions, and agricultural marketing infrastructure.
  • Total Combined Financial Outlay: ₹1,01,321.61 crore (Central Share: ₹69,088.98 crore; State Share: ₹32,232.63 crore).
  • Strategic Components Preserved: Merges 18 existing Centrally Sponsored Schemes into these two parent heads, granting states greater autonomy through District Agriculture Plans (DAPs).

MACRO • FISCAL & TAX № 2

India's External Debt Reaches $663.8 Billion; Debt-to-GDP Ratio Declines to 18.7%

  • Headline External Debt: RBI released data on India's external debt as of end-March 2024, showing total debt stood at USD 663.8 billion (an increase of USD 39.7 billion over end-March 2023).
  • Debt-to-GDP Ratio: Improved significantly, declining to 18.7% at end-March 2024 from 19.0% at end-March 2023.
  • Valuation Effect: Excluding valuation effects due to appreciation of the US dollar vis-a-vis the Indian rupee, external debt would have increased by USD 48.4 billion instead of USD 39.7 billion.
  • Currency Composition: US dollar-denominated debt remained the largest component at 53.8%, followed by the Indian rupee (31.5%), SDR (5.8%), and Japanese yen (5.4%).
  • Short-Term vs. Long-Term Debt: Long-term debt (original maturity >1 year) accounted for 81.6% of total debt; short-term debt was 18.4%.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Debt-to-GDP Ratio: Declined to 18.7% (do NOT confuse with general government debt of ~82% of GDP).
  • Currency Dominance: US Dollar (53.8%) > Indian Rupee (31.5%) > SDR (5.8%).
  • Long-Term Proportion: 81.6% of external debt is long-term.

FPI Investment Limits in Sovereign Debt & Restoration of Export Realisation Period

  • Restoration of Export Realisation Period: Reserve Bank of India restored the statutory export proceeds realisation and repatriation period to 9 months from the date of export (rolling back temporary relaxations).
  • Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) Debt Limits: • Central Government Securities (G-Secs): Overall FPI investment limit maintained at 6.0% of outstanding sovereign stock. • State Development Loans (SDLs): FPI investment limit maintained at 2.0% of outstanding state sovereign stock. • Harmonized Categories: RBI merged the General and Long-Term G-Sec categories into a single unified operational limit.
  • Fully Accessible Route (FAR) Expansion: • Expanded to include designated Government Securities with maturities of 15, 30, and 40 years. • Securities issued under the FAR route carry no foreign investment limits, supporting Indian sovereign debt integration into global benchmark indices.

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 4

RBI Financial Inclusion (FI) Index Advances to 64.2 (Zero Base Year Metric)

  • Genesis & Scope: Formally published by the Reserve Bank of India annually in July, the composite Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index) captures the extent of financial inclusion across the entire country.
  • Index Trajectory: • The composite FI-Index improved to 64.2 for March 2024 (progressing towards 70.0 in latest rounds), advancing from 60.1 in March 2023 and 43.4 in March 2017. • Growth was propelled by sustained deepening in the Quality and Usage dimensions across rural and semi-urban geographies.
  • Three Sub-Indices & Structural Weightages:
    1. Usage (45% weight): Measures active transactions in savings, credit, remittances, insurance, and pensions.
    2. Access (35% weight): Quantifies physical and digital banking infrastructure (branches, ATMs, BCs, POS terminals).
    3. Quality (20% weight): Assesses financial literacy, consumer protection, grievances, and service inequalities.
  • Unique Methodological Attribute: The FI-Index has no base year; it operates as a continuous metric bounded between 0 (complete exclusion) and 100 (complete financial inclusion).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Base Period Trap: FI-Index has NO base year (do NOT confuse with RBI-DPI which is March 2018 = 100).
  • Pillar Weights: Usage (45%) > Access (35%) > Quality (20%).
  • Scale: Continuous metric from 0 to 100.

2. 🏛️ REGULATORY BODIES NEWS

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 5

RBI Master Direction — Treatment of Wilful Defaulters and Large Defaulters (July 30)

  • Scope & Applicability: Applicable to all Scheduled Commercial Banks (incl. RRBs), All-India Financial Institutions (NABARD, EXIM, SIDBI, NHB), NBFCs, and Co-operative Banks.
  • Categorization Thresholds: • Wilful Defaulter: Borrower or guarantor with an outstanding aggregate balance of ₹25 lakh and above, who has defaulted despite having repayment capacity, siphoned/diverted funds, or disposed of charged assets without lender knowledge. • Large Defaulter: Borrower with an outstanding aggregate balance of ₹1 crore and above, whose account is classified as Doubtful or Loss (or has been resolved via compromise/suit).
  • Mandatory Timelines for Lenders: • Lenders must examine wilful default within 6 months of an account being classified as NPA. • Identification Committee (Executive Director + two senior officials) issues a reasoned show cause notice allowing 21 days for borrower response. • Review Committee (chaired by MD & CEO + two Independent Directors) confirms or cancels the classification.
  • Severe Regulatory Sanctions: • Credit Bar: Barred from availing any fresh loan/credit facility from any institutional lender for 5 years from the date their name is removed from the List of Wilful Defaulters. • Corporate Bar: Debarred from floating new ventures for 5 years and disqualified from serving as a Director on any corporate board under Section 164(2) of the Companies Act. • Compromise Settlement Restriction: No compromise or one-time settlement (OTS) allowed unless a mandatory cooling-off period of 12 months has elapsed.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Threshold Trap: Wilful Defaulter = ₹25 lakh and above; Large Defaulter = ₹1 crore and above (classic IBPS/RBI trap).
  • Timeline Trap: Lender must initiate wilful default examination within 6 months of NPA classification (not 1 year).
  • Penal Debarment: Bar on new credit is 5 years after removal of name; compromise settlement cooling-off is 12 months.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 6

RBI Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Regulated Entities (July 15)

  • Scope: Replaced the legacy 2016 framework; issued across three distinct directions for Commercial Banks (incl. RRBs), Co-operative Banks, and NBFCs.
  • Compliance with Supreme Court Mandate (SBI vs. Rajesh Agarwal, 2023): • Lenders must strictly adhere to the Principles of Natural Justice (Audi Alteram Partem — hear the other side). • Mandatory issuance of a detailed, reasoned Show Cause Notice (SCN) giving the borrower a minimum of 21 calendar days to submit a written representation before classifying an account as 'Fraud'.
  • Board-Level Oversight (SCBF): • Mandatory constitution of a Special Committee of the Board on Monitoring and Follow-up of Frauds (SCBF), comprising independent and non-executive directors. • Dedicated Fraud Monitoring Group (FMG) at the executive level.
  • Reporting & Registry Norms: • Lenders must report fraud cases to the Central Fraud Registry (CFR) within 21 days of classification. • Mandatory reporting to Law Enforcement Agencies (State Police / CBI) based on threshold: Frauds >₹3 crore by private/foreign banks to CBI/SFIO; PSU banks follow CVC guidelines.
  • Early Warning Signals (EWS): Mandatory implementation of 42 EWS indicators for all borrower credit exposures of ₹50 crore and above.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Landmark Precedent: Rooted in the Supreme Court judgment State Bank of India & Ors. vs. Rajesh Agarwal & Ors.
  • Notice Window: Minimum 21 days given to the borrower to reply to SCN before fraud classification.
  • Reporting Deadline: Classification must be uploaded to RBI's Central Fraud Registry (CFR) within 21 days.
  • EWS Exposure Threshold: Mandatory for accounts ≥₹50 crore.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 7

RBI expands Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) to IFSCs in GIFT City (July 10)

  • Policy Shift: Authorized Dealer (AD Category-I) banks are permitted to facilitate remittances by resident individuals to International Financial Services Centres (IFSCs) at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS).
  • Annual Ceilings: Retains the standard LRS cap of USD 250,000 per financial year (April–March) for permissible capital and current account transactions.
  • Expanded Scope of Permissible Usages: • Educational Expenses: Remittance for tuition fees, boarding, and living expenses to foreign university campuses approved by IFSCA (e.g., Deakin University, University of Wollongong). • Foreign Currency Accounts (FCAs): Resident individuals can open and maintain interest-bearing or non-interest-bearing FCAs in IFSC banking units (IBUs). • Financial Products & Services: Subscriptions to mutual funds, alternative investment funds (AIFs), insurance products, and debt securities issued by entities registered in GIFT City.
  • Key Prohibition: Remittances to IFSCs cannot be used for speculative trading, gambling, or round-tripping of capital.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Remittance Limit: Retains the statutory LRS ceiling of USD 250,000 per financial year.
  • New Permissible Area: Tuition/living expenses for foreign universities located directly inside GIFT City IFSC.
  • Account Type: Enables opening of Foreign Currency Accounts (FCAs) within Indian territory at IFSC units.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 8

RBI Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework for Urban Co-operative Banks (UCBs)

  • Regulatory Reach: Extended to all Primary (Urban) Co-operative Banks categorized under Tier 3 (deposits ₹100 crore to ₹1,000 crore) and Tier 4 (deposits >₹1,000 crore).
  • Three Core Financial Health Indicators:
    1. Capital Adequacy (CRAR): Mandatory minimum is 9% for Tier 3 UCBs and 12% for Tier 4 UCBs.
    2. Asset Quality (Net NPA Ratio): Breaching Net NPA > 6.0% triggers Risk Threshold 1.
    3. Profitability (Return on Assets - RoA): Negative RoA for two consecutive financial years triggers mandatory supervisory intervention.
  • Mandatory Corrective Invocations: • Risk Threshold 1: Restrictions on dividend payout/profit distribution and mandatory capital restoration plan. • Risk Threshold 2: Complete ban on opening new branches, expansion of business lines, and restriction on capital expenditure. • Risk Threshold 3: Discretionary RBI powers to supersede the Board of Directors, enforce amalgamation/merger, or cancel banking license.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Tier Applicability: Applicable only to Tier 3 and Tier 4 UCBs (deposits exceeding ₹100 crore); Tier 1 and Tier 2 UCBs are excluded.
  • Net NPA Trigger: Net NPA crossing 6.0% triggers PCA.
  • Tier 4 Capital Rule: Tier 4 UCBs must maintain minimum CRAR of 12% (vs. 9% for others).
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 9

RBI Revised Framework on Domestic Money Transfer (DMT) & Cash KYC (July 24)

  • Context: Comprehensive overhaul of domestic cash transfers through Business Correspondents (BCs), digital wallets, and prepaid payment instruments (PPIs) to curb illicit financial flows and mule accounts.
  • Mandatory Remitter Identification: • Business correspondents and banking agents cannot execute cash-to-account remittances without registering the remitter. • Mandatory verification of remitter's mobile phone number using a one-time password (OTP) and validation of Officially Valid Documents (OVD) or Aadhaar e-KYC.
  • Transaction Limits Preserved: • Maximum cash remittance limit remains ₹50,000 per month per remitter. • Single cash transaction capped at ₹5,000 for non-KYC walk-in customers at BC outlets.
  • Beneficiary Verification: Banks must include remitter identification details in the payment message (IMPS/NEFT/UPI) sent to the destination beneficiary bank to ensure end-to-end auditability.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Monthly Cash Limit: ₹50,000 per remitter per month.
  • Core Regulatory Mandate: Mandatory remitter mobile OTP verification and OVD registration for all cash remittances at BC points.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 10

RBI Directives on Dividend Declaration by Commercial Banks

  • Prudential Standards: Revised framework specifying parameters commercial banks must satisfy to declare dividends on equity shares or remit profits (in the case of foreign bank branches).
  • Three Minimum Pre-requisites:
    1. CRAR: Minimum Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio of at least 11.5% (inclusive of 2.5% Capital Conservation Buffer) for each of the preceding three financial years.
    2. Net NPA: Net NPA ratio must be less than 6.0% for the financial year for which dividend is proposed.
    3. Supervisory Compliance: Bank must comply with RBI regulations on transfer to Statutory Reserve Fund (min 20% of net profits) and provisioning.
  • Dividend Payout Ratio Matrix: • Net NPA = 0%: Maximum Dividend Payout Ratio is 50%. • Net NPA between 0% and 1%: Maximum Dividend Payout Ratio is 40%. • Net NPA between 5% and 6%: Maximum Dividend Payout Ratio is 10%.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Net NPA Ceiling: Must be <6% to be eligible for any dividend payout.
  • Minimum CRAR: Must be at least 11.5% for preceding 3 consecutive years.
  • Maximum Payout Cap: 50% of net profit (only for zero Net NPA banks).
SCIENCE & DEEP TECH № 11

Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS) & Mandatory CERSAI Registration

  • Statutory Framework: Governed under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, and the Factoring Regulation Act, 2011, providing non-recourse digital discounting of MSME trade receivables.
  • Mandatory CERSAI Registration: • All Factoring Units (invoices/bills of exchange) created and financed on TReDS platforms must be registered with CERSAI (Central Registry of Securitisation Asset Reconstruction and Security Interest of India). • Registration prevents fraudulent dual-financing or pledging of the same receivable across multiple commercial lenders.
  • Operating Platforms in India: • RXIL (Receivables Exchange of India Ltd — India's first operational TReDS exchange launched in 2016; joint venture of NSE and SIDBI). • M1xchange (Mynd Solutions Pvt. Ltd.). • Invoicemart (A.TREDS Ltd. — Axis Bank & mjunction). • C2treds (C2FO Factoring Solutions Pvt. Ltd.). • DTX (KredX Platform Pvt. Ltd.).
  • Net Worth Mandate: Existing RBI-authorized TReDS operators must meet the statutory minimum net worth requirement of ₹25 crore by March 31, 2027.
  • Eligible Participants: Buyers (corporates, CPSEs, government departments), Sellers (MSMEs), and Financiers (banks, NBFC factors).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Fraud Prevention: Mandatory registration with CERSAI eliminates duplicate invoice financing.
  • First TReDS Platform: RXIL (commenced operations in 2016; NSE + SIDBI JV).
  • Net Worth Deadline: Existing operators must achieve ₹25 crore net worth by 31 March 2027.
  • Ineligible Participants: Stock exchanges and insurance underwriters cannot participate as financiers on TReDS.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 12

RBI Recognition of Sahamati Foundation as SRO for Account Aggregator Ecosystem

  • Regulatory Milestone: Under the Omnibus Framework for Self-Regulatory Organisations (SROs), Reserve Bank of India granted formal recognition to the Sahamati Foundation as the official SRO for the Account Aggregator (AA) ecosystem.
  • Institutional Structure: • Sahamati is incorporated as a Section 8 (not-for-profit) company under the Companies Act, 2013. • Represents the collective interests of Financial Information Providers (FIPs), Financial Information Users (FIUs), and Account Aggregators (AAs).
  • Prudential SRO Governance Norms: • Application Route: Mandatory digital application submission through RBI's PRAVAAH Portal (Platform for Regulatory Application, VAlidation and AutHorisation). • Ownership Ceiling: No single member entity is permitted to hold more than 10% of the voting paid-up equity share capital to ensure neutral governance. • Net Worth Band: Prescribed minimum net worth between ₹2 crore to ₹10 crore depending on operational scale.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Designated SRO: Sahamati Foundation for the Account Aggregator network.
  • Portal for SRO Applications: RBI's PRAVAAH Portal.
  • Single Entity Ownership Cap: Maximum 10% voting shareholding; organized as a Section 8 not-for-profit entity.

4. 🌐 NATIONAL, STATE & INTERNATIONAL NEWS

DISPATCH № 17

Historic Legal Transition: Three New Criminal Laws Enacted Nationwide (July 1)

  • Enforcement Date: Three transformative criminal law statutes came into full legal effect across India on July 1, 2024, completely repealing and replacing British colonial-era penal codes:
    1. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (BNS): Replaced the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).
    2. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS): Replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC).
    3. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (BSA): Replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
  • Key Judicial Innovations: • Mandates Zero FIR (can be filed at any police station irrespective of jurisdiction). • Introduction of e-FIR and compulsory electronic summons via SMS/WhatsApp. • Mandatory audio-video recording of search and seizure operations, and mandatory forensic investigation for offences punishable by 7 years or more. • Introduction of Community Service as a recognized formal penal punishment for minor offences.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Enforcement Date: July 1, 2024 (not Jan 1 or April 1).
  • Statutory Cross-Mapping: BNS = IPC; BNSS = CrPC; BSA = Evidence Act.
  • Forensic Threshold: Mandatory for offences carrying imprisonment of 7 years or more.

Union Cabinet approves ₹76,220 Crore Mega Major Port at Vadhavan, Maharashtra

  • Top 10 Global Target: Designed with a natural draft of 20 meters, capable of handling the world's largest container mega-vessels (up to 24,000 TEUs); target cumulative capacity of 298 million metric tonnes (MMT) per annum, propelling India into the Top 10 container ports globally.

DISPATCH № 19

Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act & Implementing Rules Enacted

  • Statutory Enforcement: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions operationalized the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 and notified its comprehensive implementing rules nationwide.
  • Examinations & Bodies Covered: • Covers competitive examinations conducted by Union Public Service Commission (UPSC), Staff Selection Commission (SSC), Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs), National Testing Agency (NTA), and the Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS).
  • Penal Slabs & Liability Architecture: • Individual Malpractices: Persons resorting to unfair means face imprisonment of 3 to 5 years and a fine up to ₹10 lakh. • Organized Paper Leak Syndicates: Imprisonment of 5 to 10 years and a mandatory minimum fine of ₹1 crore. • Service Provider Penalty: Examination conducting agencies/service providers found complicit face recovery of full examination costs and a complete bar from conducting public examinations for 4 years. • Legal Character: All offences under the statute are non-bailable, cognizable, and non-compoundable.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE
  • Banking Exam Coverage: Explicitly governs IBPS examinations alongside UPSC, SSC, and NTA.
  • Organized Syndicate Penalties: Minimum fine of ₹1 Crore; 5 to 10 years imprisonment.
  • Legal Classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable offences.

Prudential Guidelines on Project Finance — Construction Phase Debt (RBI Exposure Draft)

  • Context: Standard prudential guidelines for financing infrastructure and non-infrastructure project loans during the pre-commissioning phase.
  • Graduated Provisioning Architecture: • Construction Phase (Under-Construction): Proposed standard asset provisioning stepped up to 5.0% (up from current baseline of 0.4%) in a phased manner (2% by FY25, 3.5% by FY26, 5% by FY27). • Operational Phase (Post-DCCO): Once the project achieves Date of Commencement of Commercial Operations (DCCO), provisioning drops to 2.5%. • Stabilization Phase: Drops further to 1.0% once the project generates sufficient positive free cash flow and repays at least 20% of its long-term debt.
  • Financial Closure Deadline: Financial closure must be achieved within 1 year from the date of sanction for infrastructure projects.
